newsitem.title: GERMANY: SGL Carbon still sees 1997 profit rise.
newsitem.headline: SGL Carbon still sees 1997 profit rise.

text.p: Germany's SGL Carbon AG said on Tuesday it was maintaining its forecast for a double-digit percentage rise in 1997 despite a nine percent drop in first quarter pre-tax profit.
The leading carbon and graphite maker said group pre-tax profit fell to 71 million marks in the first three months of 1997 from 78 million marks in the year-earlier period.
The company said it had expected a weak start to the year because of several one-off factors and weakness in the European steel industry.
Net profit fell 11 percent to 43 million marks in the first quarter from 48 million, the company said in a statement.

"Our order books make us very confident for the second quarter," SGL said in a statement. Looking ahead to the full year, the company reiterated previous forecasts, saying: "Barring unforeseen circumstances we expect an earnings improvement by a double-digit percentage rate which clearly exceeds sales growth."

The company said business in graphite electrodes in Europe was picking up and that its profit outlook seemed realistic even though it expected one-time costs of 25 million marks for rationalisation measures and the integration of acquisitions.

Referring to the decline in first-quarter pre-tax profit, SGL noted that income was burdened by the cost of management share schemes, lower income from non-consolidated companies and increased interest payments resulting from acquisitions.
Group operating profit in the first quarter remained unchanged at 80 million marks, SGL said.
